title: feat(spec,service-automation,lint)!: a CRUD node's filter operands are value slots, the query placeholders stay — the {…} token refused (#19939 pass 4, S6)
body:
Part of #19939
Clause-②: yes (narrowing: a flow {…} token at a get_record, update_record or delete_record filter operand is refused, a whole-string query placeholder excepted, an object naming a string dialect at an operand must be a valid CEL value envelope, an operand envelope that evaluates to null refuses the node, and @objectstack/lint no longer exports validateFlowFilterTokens, FLOW_FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN or FlowFilterTokenFinding and retires the flow-filter-token-unknown rule id; widening: a filter operand gains the CEL value envelope arm, the exported FlowNodeExpressionPath type gains the optional filterOperands field, ValueSlotTemplateOptions gains filterOperand, FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS gains the three filter rows, LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS gains get_record and delete_record, the published GetRecordConfig, UpdateRecordConfig and DeleteRecordConfig JSON Schemas mark filter as a value slot, and flowFilterOperands, FlowFilterOperand, classifyFlowFilterOperandString and FlowFilterOperandStringKind are new exports)

Pass 4, stage S6 of #19939: the CRUD filter operands, under Fork R17 → **A** (stage plan `6096263424`). S7 follows, so this PR does not close the card.

Each operand of a `get_record`, `update_record` or `delete_record` node's `filter` is now a value slot. That covers a field's value, an operator's comparand and each element of a list comparand, at any depth of `$and` / `$or` / `$not` and of a nested-relation condition. An operand takes one of three forms:

- **A CEL value envelope.** The executor evaluates it in the run's scope before the query.
- **A query placeholder** (`{current_user_id}`, `{today}`, `{30_days_ago}`, … from `data/context-tokens.zod.ts`). It is handed to the query engine untouched, as before.
- **A literal.**

Every other single-brace `{…}` token at an operand is refused at every door, and the refusal names the envelope to write instead. The `#3810` guard holds for an envelope that evaluates to `null` or `undefined`: the node is refused, and nothing is queried.

## FROM → TO, per position

The positions are the `filter` of `get_record`, `update_record` and `delete_record`. Within each filter, the operand positions are:

| operand position | FROM (the template) | TO |
|:--|:--|:--|
| a field's value | `{ id: '{record.id}' }` | `{ id: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.id' } }` |
| an operator's comparand | `{ amount: { $gt: '{record.cap}' } }` | `{ amount: { $gt: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.cap' } } }` |
| a list comparand's element | `{ id: { $in: ['{a}', '{b}'] } }` | `{ id: { $in: [{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'a' }, { dialect: 'cel', source: 'b' }] } }`, or one envelope evaluating to the list |
| a computed combinator member | `{ $and: '{record.conds}' }` | `{ $and: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.conds' } }` (one operand; the stored-metadata refusal still judges what it evaluates to) |
| a nested-relation condition | `{ account: { owner: '{x}' } }` | `{ account: { owner: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'x' } } }` |
| the run user | `{ owner: '{$User.Id}' }` | `{ owner: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'current_user.id' } }`, behind a `decision` on `current_user != null` |
| a date macro | `{ due: { $lt: '{TODAY() - 3}' } }` | `{ due: { $lt: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'isoDate(daysAgo(3))' } } }` |
| a query placeholder | `{ owner: '{current_user_id}' }`, `{ due: { $lt: '{today}' } }` | **unchanged** |
| a variable named like a placeholder | `'{today}'` (the variable shadowed the placeholder) | `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'today' }`; `'{today}'` is now always the placeholder |

Each FROM row is refused at `objectstack validate`, at `registerFlow`, at the metadata save door and at the executor's parse, located at the operand (`config.filter.id.$in[1]`), with the envelope as the remedy. Each TO row passes all four doors.

## Census, per shape (base `6662e3f59`, a TypeScript AST walk over every tracked `.ts`/`.js` file plus a `git grep` over `.md`/`.mdx`/`.json`/`.yaml`)

| shape | shipped (examples, docs, dogfood, spec text) | tests | after this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| a field's value, flow token | 7 in examples (`app-crm` 2, `app-showcase` 3, `app-todo` 2); 6 in dogfood (5 files); 5 in docs (`common-patterns` 1, `kernel/runtime-services/examples` 2, `service-automation` README 2); the flows guide's `{uid}` row; 2 spec remedy texts (`CRUD_RECORD_ID_GUIDANCE`, the run-user remedy); the `FlowSchema` example | about 87 real flow tokens in 34 files | all migrated, except 14 in `validate-flow-template-paths.test.ts` and 1 in `reference-integrity-suite.test.ts`, which S7 owns, and 3 in the deleted rule's test |
| an operator's comparand | query placeholders only: 1 (`app-todo` `{3_days_ago}`) | 2 placeholders; 1 flow token (`{record.guess}` through a helper argument) | placeholders unchanged; the token migrated |
| a combinator member, computed | 0 | 1 (`$and: '{record.conds}'`) | migrated to an envelope |
| a list comparand's element | 0 | 0 | — |
| a nested-relation condition | 0 | 0 | — |
| text with holes at an operand | 0 | 0 | — |
| a whole-string query placeholder | `app-todo` `{tomorrow}`, `{3_days_ago}` | `{90_days_ago}` (`flow.test.ts`), the door controls | unchanged, pinned as positive controls |

A flow variable or output variable named like a placeholder: 0 in the repository. An object declaring a field named `dialect`: 0. hotcrm was not measured.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

- **A1 holds.** At the base, `interpolateFilter` had exactly one caller, `crud-nodes.ts:104` (`resolveNodeFilter`), reached by `get_record`, `update_record` and `delete_record`. No other executor read a filter through it or an equivalent. The three schemas carried `filter: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()`. All three are now `flowFilterSlotSchema`, and `GetRecordConfigSchema` and `DeleteRecordConfigSchema` join `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`.
- **A2, one classifier.** There were two grammars:
  - At the base, the executor resolved a whole token against the variables first, and only an unresolved known placeholder survived.
  - The lint rule classified through `flow-template-grammar`'s own table.

  Now `classifyFlowFilterOperandString` in `@objectstack/spec/automation` draws the line, using `FILTER_TOKEN_WRAPPED_RE` and `isKnownFilterToken`. A whole wrapped known token is `placeholder`. Any other string carrying a token is `flow-token`. The rest is `literal`.

  The contract, `registerFlow`, `objectstack validate`, the save door and the executor's parse all read it, through the value-slot judge in its filter mode. The executor does not classify strings itself: it evaluates envelopes and hands everything else on as written, after the parse has refused the tokens. The lint rule `flow-filter-token-unknown` retires; see below.

  On shadowing: a flow variable named like a placeholder no longer shadows it, and the variable is read through an envelope. Zero instances were measured; the change is pinned in `crud-filter-guard.test.ts`.
- **A3 holds.** An operand envelope that evaluates to `null` or `undefined` refuses the node as a guard (`errorClass: 'guard'`; a `fault` edge cannot route it), and nothing is queried:
  - The step error code is `NODE_FAILURE`, pinned on `update_record`, `delete_record` and `get_record`.
  - It is pinned per position (comparand, list element, `$or` member) and for a partial filter.
  - An absent variable or key fails the run before any query with `EXECUTION_ERROR`, naming it.
  - A literal `null` operand is an authored IS NULL condition and is handed on.
- **A4.** The census above.
- **A5, no fork.** An envelope is an object whose `dialect` is a string. At an operand position, an object is either an operator map (`$` keys) or a nested-relation condition, and neither names a string `dialect`. The one ambiguous spelling is a nested-relation condition on a related field named `dialect`. It is written `{ dialect: { $eq: 'x' } }`, which is unambiguous. No object in the repository declares such a field.

## The lint rule `flow-filter-token-unknown` retires (a choice settled in-stage, flagged for the seat)

The rule reported a `{FUNC()}` filter token that neither dialect resolves. Every token it reported is now refused by the value-slot judge, at the same doors (save door included), at the same severity and position, and with the envelope remedy instead of the retired dialect's. Keeping the rule would report one defect twice, with two remedies. The four axes:

1. **Business need:** zero shipped uses. Its one-line `fix:` (merged in #23097) teaches a single-brace spelling that is now refused.
2. **Long-term soundness:** one judge per position, with no second grammar (order A2).
3. **Preventing AI mistakes:** the refusal stays as loud, stays at the same doors and names the right remedy.
4. **Startup focus:** retired at once, with no dual window.

The rule, its `os explain` entry and its three exports are removed. The `os validate` and `os build` transcripts now count 49 author-time rules.

## ADR-0087

The step-18 D3 entry `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` is amended:

- **surface:** each CRUD filter operand.
- **replacement:** the envelope, the placeholders, null, and the `dialect` escape.
- **reason:** shadowing; an erased condition against a run fault.
- **acceptance:** re-run the queries and compare the rows matched.

There is no new entry, no D2 conversion (no lossless spelling: a whole token that resolved to nothing refused the node, where CEL faults on an absent root) and no tombstone.

Every shipped example, doc and dogfood site is an envelope or a query placeholder.

## Acceptance notes

- **S7's single-brace readers, left as the scope fence says.**
  - `validate-flow-template-paths` still path-checks a single-brace token at a filter operand. Its test keeps 14 such fixtures, and `reference-integrity-suite.test.ts` keeps 1. They pass because that rule reads the single-brace body, and S7 retires that reading. Carrier: S7.
  - The lint's bare-`$` hint arm ("Wrap it and bind a variable: `{x}`") is now reachable only at a position no slot judges, such as a plugin node's own config. No builtin position reaches it. Carrier: S7.
- **The lookup-hop remedy at this position is gone.**
  - The template's guard message ended "a relation field holds a scalar id — a lookup hop needs the relation in the start node's `config.expand`".
  - Under CEL, a hop through a scalar id (`record.account.name`) faults in `evaluateValueEnvelope`. It gets the engine's generic evaluation message, the same as every other value slot since S1, so that clause no longer prints here. A null result still refuses the node, with the guard's message.
  - Carrier: none. It is noted, not filed: it is wording on the family's engine-wide fault text.
- **Text that still names the retired rule or the single brace (seat-carried or release-owned).**
  - `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md:168` names `flow-filter-token-unknown`. That is skill text, which the seat carries with its #22585 pointer.
  - Pending changesets on this line that this PR makes false. They are not edited here (one changeset per stage); they are offered for an in-place correction like #23126:
    - `.changeset/19939-flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused.md` says "A `filter` value keeps the template dialect". After this PR, a filter operand is a value slot too.
    - `.changeset/19939-flow-value-slot-run-user-refused.md` (the `$User.Email` row) names `filter: { id: '{uid}' }`. It should read `filter: { id: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'current_user.id' } }`, with no assignment step. This changeset already says it supersedes that line.
    - `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-10-one-line.md` and `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-14-one-line-fix.md` describe `flow-filter-token-unknown`'s message and one-line fix, for a rule this PR retires in the same release.
  - The migration registry's step-18 text-slot entry (`registry.ts.template`, `flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused`) still says "Every other flow string keeps the single-brace dialect". It has been left alone, as S1–S5 left it. Carrier: S7, which deletes the resolver.
- **The inert value arm.**
  - The first cut added a `filterOperands` branch to `atOrInsideJudgedLedgerSlot`. Its ablation stayed green: `insideValueSlot` already leaves every issue under a ledger value slot to the envelope pass and the judge, and the new `filter` rows bring each operand under one.
  - The branch was removed in `7edc95fa5`. The pin "one finding, never two" stays, held by the ledger rows.
- **A local-only red that is not this change.** Four spec repo-project tree walks read the gitignored `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/`, which the `@objectstack/docs` build writes through `gen:upgrade-guide`:
  - `export-job-family-retirement`, `compliance-families-retirement`, `connector-connection-timeout-retirement` and `currency-mode-family-closure` rule B.
  - With the generated tree present they are red on retired names quoted in `18.md`. With it set aside they are 4/4 green. Reported to the seat as a finding.
- **A pre-existing dogfood red.** At the merge base, `view-container-cross-package-default.dogfood.test.ts` was red (DELETE `/meta/view/…` answered 400). Main fixed the test in #23105 (`2808438e9`). On the merged head the file is green (1/1).
- **Not measured:**
  - hotcrm, which lives in another repository.
  - `pnpm check:type-check-debt`, which the dispatch rules out.
  - The objectui designer's single-brace filter pickers, carried by the seat's companion card.
